exposure: Etiology of genitourinary fistula (iatrogenic vs. ischemic)
outcome: Trends in fistula etiology over time
cohort: The study included 909 women diagnosed with genitourinary fistula presenting for management in Kigali, Rwanda.
finding: There was a significant increase in iatrogenic genitourinary fistula over a 10-year period in Rwanda, comprising 46% of all diagnosed fistulas, and these were more likely to require invasive surgical approaches.
mod_finding: Iatrogenic fistula were defined as those temporally following cesarean section or hysterectomy, indicating a link between specific surgical modes of birth/gynecological procedures and fistula etiology.
